The spec already positions the deterministic regex scan (§4.5 pre-cache injection scan) as the primary security gate, running BEFORE both cache lookup and the LLM bouncer. The LLM bouncer is a secondary gate, not the primary boundary. All critical injection-pattern rejection cases are covered by the deterministic scan. The recommendation to make some bouncer tests build-blocking is a valid enhancement but not an architectural defect — the mocked-test + canary approach is a documented and accepted trade-off for hackathon scope. Phonetic evasion is explicitly acknowledged as a known gap with a v1.5 fix path.

SPEC-07 §10.1 mandatory scope explicitly specifies '300-row demo seed corpus (from CAD_VOCAB_CORPUS.md §4)' — the 22-row materials demo slice, not the full 19k catalog. The full catalog is Phase 3 (CAD_VOCAB_CORPUS.md §6) with explicit licensing review noted in §7. This is project-management scoping documented in the corpus manifest, not an architecture defect. The v1.0 Medtronic work is explicitly Tier 2, post-hackathon.

Previously accepted in Round 1 but text revision was not applied. SPEC-02 §9.0.2 pseudocode uses Guid.CreateVersion7() which requires .NET 9+; add-in targets .NET Framework 4.8. Applying fix now: add UUIDv7 polyfill note.

architectural_risks_remaining: Non-atomic citation persistence: a committed turn can exist without its vocabulary-resolution decoration if the decoration write fails. The compensating control (session lock on circuit-breaker open) bounds blast radius to one uncited turn per failure episode.

SPEC-05 contract undefined: the DhfDecorationPersister that SPEC-05 must implement (SDR-07-012, Seam E₂) is still TBD. The seam is documented but the implementation contract remains a gap until SPEC-05 is authored.

NetFx HTTP status observability: the fix provides workaround guidance but does not eliminate the fundamental limitation of .NET Framework 4.8 ClientWebSocket. Day-0 validation must confirm the chosen extraction approach.

LLM bouncer stochasticity: the bouncer is an LLM call subject to model updates and prompt drift. The deterministic pre-cache scan is the primary gate; the bouncer is secondary. Build-breaking tests use recorded responses only.
